rows.10:4f80:
Feels nice, doesn't it?
The summer wind is warm and muggy, and truly pleasant.
Come, {a}{f:.|.}
Why don't you try it too?
Look down from this roof.
From barely a dozen meters up, people already look like ants, don't they?
Wouldn't you like to give yourself to this school as well?
What do you say?
Wouldn't you like to be free of it all?
Wouldn't you like to depart?{p}Just like Aizawa did...
rows.10:5100: I have no intention of departing
rows.10:5114:
...I see.
Perhaps it's still too early for you.{p}
rows.10:5154:
Oh yes, I promised to let you meet Aizawa.
Meeting Aizawa is easy, you know.
You just say this:
"Aizawa, let's begin the experiment."{p}Simple, isn't it?
rows.10:5214:
"So if I say it, I'll get to meet him?"
{f:I|I} asked him back.{p}
rows.10:526c:
Arai's eyes looked as if they were gazing at something far away.
The three who hadn't told their stories yet silently watched the exchange between Arai and {f:me|me}.
"Arai.
May I ask you one thing?
What is it that's in this school?
What are you saying everyone is possessed by?"{p}
rows.10:5380:
Arai gave a broad smile.
"Say it, please. Say those words.
Then you might understand."
It was true: something was in this school.
{f:I|I} {f:had sensed it myself|could sense it too}.
{f:I|I} nodded at Arai's words.
And then... I said it.
"Aizawa.
Let's begin the experiment!"
It happened in that very instant.{p}
rows.10:5578:
"Look out!"
Before {f:I|I} could even reach out, Arai's body was flying through the air.{p}
rows.10:56e4:
"Ah!"
A huge skull, so vast it covered the whole sky, was floating up there.
{f:Was that|Could that be} what Arai had pointed at?
"...Is that Aizawa?"{p}
rows.10:57a0:
The skull vanished in an instant.
Before I knew it, the three who were left had gathered around {f:me|me}.
"What now? Three of 'em have vanished on us.
You still gonna keep this going?"
One of them said it.
What should I do?
I never dreamed it would come to this.
Maybe I could still turn back now.
If I kept on like this, I felt I'd only sink in deeper...
I couldn't shake that feeling.
Was what was happening around {f:me|me} right now real...
Or was it an illusion...{p}Should I really keep going like this{f:?|?}
rows.10:59b0:
"Let's do it.
...If it's all right with all of you.
I feel like we can't let it end like this."
The three nodded in silence.{p}
rows.10:5a34:
And so {f:we|we} left the roof and {f:went back|decided to go back} to the newspaper club room.
{f:I|I} hoped nothing would happen during the fourth story...{p}
rows.10:5ad8:
I see.
It's true that when you're healthy, you probably don't think people die all that easily.
Then let's shift the topic a little, toward life and death.{p}{a}{f:,|,} you get scared when you climb up somewhere high, don't you?
rows.10:5cb4:
His name was Uehara, and he often bragged about how brave he was.
He'd sit at the window in dangerous poses; even in little everyday things, he loved to do something risky.
He was on the rugby team.
And on that team, something like this happened.
"If you jump off the roof and live, I'll make you a starter on the spot."
That's what an upperclassman on the rugby team said to the new members.
Of course, he must have figured no one would ever do it.
The juniors were stung.
"Hey, Uehara, you do it."
"Come on, you'd die, no matter what."
"Jumping off the roof isn't a question of guts or stamina.
You'd die for sure."{p}
rows.10:5f00:
"But it's galling, isn't it? Him saying that 'cause he thinks we can't do it."
Uehara listened to their talk in silence.
Of course, both the upperclassman and Uehara's friends had only said it as a joke.
No one would ever actually do such a thing.
But from then on, Uehara couldn't get the idea of jumping off the roof out of his head.
(Would I really die for sure?)
Uehara couldn't stop wondering about it.
Whenever he had a spare moment, he started going to the roof to look down at the ground.{p}
rows.10:60ac:
One time, he climbed over the railing and went outside it.
Outside the railing, there was a ledge only a dozen or so centimeters wide.
"Whoaaa, this feels amazing!"
Uehara felt a thrill he had never known before.
After that, he often went out past the railing on the roof.{p}
rows.10:61b8:
"Announcing the starters.........."
The rugby team's starters were announced.
"Uehara, ......."
He had made the starting lineup as a first-year.
"Uehara, you earned that spot on your own merit.
So quit going up to the roof now."
"Oh... okay."
Everyone on the team laughed.
But Uehara didn't stop going up to the roof.{p}
rows.10:630c:
Then one day, a corpse was found in the water tank on the roof, and the roof was off-limits for a while.
Uehara was dying to go up there.{p}
rows.10:63b4:
One night, he finally snuck into the school and went up to the roof.
After so long, the roof felt exhilarating.
Then he climbed over the railing and stepped outside it.
"I want to stay here forever."
Uehara murmured that to himself.{p}
rows.10:647c:
And then he quietly stood up and jumped.
It was an exhilaration unlike anything he had ever felt.
And as he felt death, he realized it clearly:
he had wanted to die all along.{p}
rows.10:6540:
He died.
If you jump off the roof of the new school building, you die.
That's why he liked being on the roof, you see.
Feeling death was a joy to him.
After that incident, the roof was off-limits for a while.
But why don't you try sneaking up there sometime?
I hear Uehara is there.
They say he jumps off the roof every night.
And when someone comes, they say Uehara tells them this:
"Let's jump together."{p}And that's the end of my story.
Next, please.{p}
rows.10:6798:
This time, rather than fear, I'd like to tell you about someone who had little sense of the worth of life.
Though high schoolers these days seem to lean that way a bit, too.
They say it's because, with nuclear families and housing conditions and so on, many people have never seen a relative or a pet die up close.
That's why so many juvenile crimes lately are so cruel, or so the story goes.
People actually die surprisingly easily, though.
I used to be the same as you, {a}{f:,|,} and never gave death a thought.
But the incident I'm about to tell you made me start thinking about life.{p}
rows.10:6994:
There was a student who could kill the animals in the school's animal hutch without batting an eye.
Each time, a teacher scolded him, but the lectures appealed to his feelings, so he couldn't understand the scolding at all.
"Morikawa, don't you feel sorry for them?"
"Sorry."
To him, it felt like no more than breaking some school equipment.
"You eat meat and fish yourself, don't you? Then quit eating it."
He looked like he wanted to say something like that.
Even on his way home, if he found a handy little animal, he would torment it to death.{p}
rows.10:6b78:
Then one day, Yoko Nakayama, a girl in his class, brought her pet hamster to school.
"Yoko, it's so cute!"
"You'll be in big trouble if the teacher finds out."
"Let's all keep it safe."
Everyone doted on the hamster.{p}
rows.10:6c5c: But when Morikawa saw that hamster, he wanted to torment it.{p}
rows.10:6ca4:
At first, he held back.
"Come on, it's Nakayama's pet, after all."
But holding back only made the urge grow stronger.
Morikawa waited for his chance.
Third period ended.{p}
rows.10:6d9c:
Several girls gathered around Nakayama.
"Next is P.E."
"Yoko, what are you going to do with the hamster?"
"It'll be fine. It'll stay quiet in my bag for an hour or so."
Talking like that, they headed off to the changing room.{p}
rows.10:6f50:
The classroom was dead silent; faint voices drifted in from the class next door.
After making sure there was no one in the hallway, Morikawa went over to Nakayama's desk.{p}
rows.10:6fe8:
Then he opened her bag and took out the hamster.
He tormented it mercilessly until it was dead.{p}What do you think he did with the hamster after that?
rows.10:7088: He threw it in the trash
rows.10:7098: He put it back in the bag
rows.10:7140:
When he got back, Nakayama's class was in an uproar.
Of course, Morikawa knew why, but he asked,
"What's going on?"
just the same.
"Nakayama's hamster's gone missing."
"Everyone, let's help look for it."
Someone suggested that, so they started searching.
"It's not here. Maybe it got out of the room."
"Guys, the teacher's coming!"
When someone said that, everyone stopped searching.{p}
rows.10:7364:
But the hamster wasn't found, and school let out.
"Where could my hamster have gone?"
Nakayama said, worried.
"Let's do the cleaning.
If we look while we clean, I'm sure we'll find it."
The girl on cleaning duty with her that day tried to cheer her up.{p}
rows.10:7470:
As everyone else went home, a few stayed behind to start cleaning, and Morikawa was among them.
(Crap. I've gotta go dump the hamster in the trash can, fast.)
Thinking that, he casually went to get the trash can.
"Yoko, I'll take the trash out to the incinerator."
He'd been beaten to it.
"Yoshioka, I'll go, so you help her look for the hamster."
"Oh, thanks."
With that, Morikawa took over taking out the trash.{p}
rows.10:7608:
Morikawa picked up the trash can and headed for the incinerator.
When he got there, he tossed in the trash and the hamster.
Then he piled trash over the hamster.
(That should do it.)
Just as he thought that and turned to head back to the classroom...{p}
rows.10:76f0:
"So it was you after all."
It was Nakayama.
"I can't believe it was really killed..."
"It's not like that.
I thought you'd be sad if you found out it was dead..."
"Liar!"{p}What do you think Morikawa did then?
rows.10:77f4:
That's right, he kept up the lie.
"I don't know anything about it.
I just thought you'd be sad if I showed it to you."
That's what Morikawa said.
Nakayama ran to the hamster and held it in her arms.
He walked away from there.{p}
rows.10:78d0:
From the next day on, Nakayama stopped coming to school.
Morikawa was racked with guilt, but
"It's just a little animal that cost a few hundred yen,"
he told himself as an excuse, or so I heard.{p}
rows.10:7990:
Some time later, when he'd almost forgotten about it, Nakayama, who had been absent all that time, was waiting for him near Morikawa's house.
"Long time no see."
"Nakayama..."
"Lately, I've started to understand how you feel.
Look..."{p}
rows.10:7a74:
Nakayama opened her bag, and inside were the carcasses of dozens of small animals.
"Well?"
Hamsters and other creatures, lots of them, lay dead with their eyes wide open.
The carcasses, which shouldn't have been seeing anything, seemed to be staring at Morikawa, accusing him.
Even Morikawa felt sick.
"Ugh... urk."
What was in his stomach slowly crept up his throat.{p}
rows.10:7cd8:
That night, he had no appetite at all.
The sight of the carcasses Nakayama had shown him wouldn't leave his mind.
They say he didn't touch a bite of the hamburger steak he usually loved.
He went back to his room early and went straight to bed.
I wonder how long he had been asleep.
A noise woke him up.{p}
rows.10:7e08:
"Geez, I'm trying to sleep. Keep it down."
Thinking it was the TV, Morikawa went to the living room to complain.
The living room lights were off; it was pitch dark.
When he looked at the clock again, it was three in the morning.
(Nobody'd be watching TV at this hour.
...So what was that?){p}
rows.10:7fa0:
This time, he could tell for certain that the noise was coming from inside his own house.
He moved forward, straining his ears.{p}
rows.10:8024:
(Something's coming from this room...)
It was his parents' room.
(Are Mom and Dad still up?
What are they doing?){p}
rows.10:8174:
In the darkness, something like a cord was moving.
"Nakayama... you...!"
She was strangling his parents with a rope.
"Oh my, I said I'd tell you later, but you just couldn't wait...?
You know, it's the best, killing people.
With animals, you were my senior, but now I'm the one ahead.
Oh, that's right.
To thank you, I'll teach you how to kill a person.
Heh heh, heh... heh..."
Morikawa tried to lunge at Nakayama.{p}
rows.10:8314:
At that moment, his murdered mother's head lolled over to face him.
"Ugh..."
His mother's face was twisted in agony, and her eyes looked terribly sad, they say.
...Morikawa passed out.{p}
rows.10:83e0:
The next day, when Morikawa didn't come to school, his teacher got worried and came to his house.
But no matter how many times the teacher rang the doorbell, no one answered.
There were traces of blood at the front door.
Thinking it strange, the teacher called the police, apparently.{p}
rows.10:84b8:
...Morikawa was in his parents' room.
They say he had laid his parents' bodies out neatly side by side, and was sitting next to them, staring blankly.
At first, Morikawa was investigated as a suspect, but he was soon cleared.
But he had become so unstable that he had to be put in a hospital.
Did they catch the killer, you ask?
No, not yet.
Morikawa said that Nakayama was the one who did it, but...
The police didn't believe him; they said it was a crime no girl could possibly commit.{p}
rows.10:8860:
That's right, he told her the truth.
"But it's just a hamster.
They're not that expensive, right?
I'll pay you back for it sometime."
With that, Morikawa walked away.{p}
rows.10:8904:
The next day, she was absent from school.
"Morikawa, Nakayama's out today, huh.{p}Guess losing her hamster was a real shock to her."
